title: AeroScale Systems x Redwood - channel + GPU partnership discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and AeroScale to explore channel/reseller alignment and a potential joint offering: AeroScale to provide managed GPU pools and edge onramps for Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments. Discussed integration touchpoints (XLA/driver support, VPC peering, billing flows), high-level SSO/KMS/compliance questions, and next steps for NDA + technical deep-dive and benchmark plan.
topics: GPU hardware mix and driver compatibility
action_items: Alex Nguyen: circulate partnership one-pager + Redwood partner NDA by 2026-12-03
Priya Patel: share a short integration checklist (driver versions, CUDA/cuDNN, AMI recommendations) by 2026-12-07
Ibrahim Al-Karim: provide AeroScale hardware inventory + rack-level specs and expected availability window by 2026-12-06
Michael Chen & Sam Carter: coordinate pilot commercial model options (rev share vs. discounted resale) and email summary by 2026-12-10

Schedule 90-min technical deep-dive (Redwood SE + AeroScale infra leads)

transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-11-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording enabled)
Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Sam Carter (Redwood Product), Michael Chen (AeroScale Head of Partnerships), Laura Gomez (AeroScale Cloud Architect), Ibrahim Al-Karim (AeroScale GPU Ops Lead), Sofia Ruiz (AeroScale Legal Ops)

--- Summary (auto) ---
Quick intro, alignment on partnership models (reseller/referral/channel), high-level technical constraints around drivers and private network topologies, security/compliance checklist items, and agreed pilot/benchmark next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, I think we have about 45, 50 minutes on the calendar. I'll kick off with a quick intro to Redwood and then hand to Priya for the technical bits. Michael, thanks for coordinating.
[00:18] Michael Chen: Yeah, thanks Alex. Appreciate you, um, making time. Super excited, we've been talking about, you know, expanding our channel for enterprise inference.
[00:30] Alex Nguyen: Great. Quick introductions? Real quick, I'm Alex, AE focused on partnerships and channel. Priya is our systems SE who owns private and dedicated deployments. Sam is product and will help with go-to-market. Priya?
[00:45] Priya Patel: Hi all. Priya Patel, I work on Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments — networking, autoscaling, and performance. Happy to dig into ops/compat.
[00:58] Laura Gomez: Laura — Cloud Architect at AeroScale, I look after the AMI images, driver ops, and the cloud footprint. Ibrahim sits on GPU ops.
[01:10] Ibrahim Al-Karim: Hi, Ibrahim. I run the rack and firmware side — like provisioning, driver testing, and capacity windows.
[01:20] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, I'm on legal, happy to help with NDAs and partner contract questions.
[01:27] Alex Nguyen: Cool. The goal for today is to see where our integration points are — the channel model you prefer, what the technical integration will look like, and agree a pilot. We'll be pretty pragmatic.
[01:40] Michael Chen: Sounds good. For background: AeroScale runs managed GPU pools across 6 regions, we do both centralized cloud and edge colocation. We want to resell or embed Redwood inference — customers want low-latency inference near edge sites.
[01:56] Priya Patel: Nice. Two quick clarifying q's: 1) do you plan to host Redwood control plane or use our hosted API and just route inference traffic to your pools? 2) how are you thinking about billing / metering?
[02:12] Michael Chen: Our preference is to be a reseller — customers buy through AeroScale, billing through us, but we'd like the control plane to be Redwood-managed at first. For bigger enterprise deals we might want a private control plane on our VPC. For metering, we can do a usage meter at the infra level or pass-through to Redwood's metering API.
[02:33] Alex Nguyen: Okay — reseller model + hosted control plane initially is pretty common. We can do both: hosted API for onboarding and then support Private deployments with VPC peering when customers require it.
[02:46] Sam Carter: From product POV we want to make sure the rollout story is clean — like the customer sees AeroScale as the procurement path but the runtime is still Redwood-managed unless they opt for private.
[02:57] Ibrahim Al-Karim: On the infra side: our GPUs are mixed — A800-ish x1, H100, and a bunch of A100 older racks. We do firmware updates monthly. Curious about model compatibility — is Redwood doing quantization/ops that require specific driver versions?
[03:18] Priya Patel: Good question. Redwood's runtime supports int8/4 quant paths and we have optimizations that prefer recent CUDA and driver stacks. Practically, for best perf we recommend Nvidia driver >=535 and CUDA 12.x for H100 patterns; older A100s can work on 470 with some perf compromise. We'll share a matrix.
[03:36] Laura Gomez: Okay that helps. We'll need a compatibility matrix because we run customers on different racks.
[03:42] Priya Patel: We'll send a short checklist with exact versions — think of it like: recommended/compatible/unsupported.
[03:50] Michael Chen: On networking, our customers often require direct VPC peering or private link. Does Redwood support VPC peering for Redwood Private? And for Dedicated, can we integrate with your SDN?
[04:04] Alex Nguyen: Yes — for Redwood Private we can deploy a control plane into your VPC or set up VPC peering; for Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) we can set routing policies and peering arrangements. There are options: full private control plane, or partner-managed gateway that routes to Redwood hosted control plane. Priya, thoughts on topology?
[04:22] Priya Patel: Topologies vary. For low-latency edge, we often do a hybrid: control plane in Redwood-hosted but edge workers in partner-managed VPCs with secure tunnels and mTLS. For fully private, we install the control plane into your VPC and we use SAML/OIDC for SSO. We'll show diagrams in the deep-dive.
[04:40] Ibrahim Al-Karim: And for KV cache and model weights — do we need shared NFS? How do you manage model artifacts?
[04:50] Priya Patel: Model artifacts can be pulled to local fast storage on the nodes; for some setups we use an object store with signed presigned urls. KV cache is in-memory per instance with optional prefix caching that can be snapshotted to S3 for warm starts. That's what we usually recommend for edge.
[05:07] Alex Nguyen: Also to be transparent — we have an Optimize product that suggests batching and quantization settings per workload; partners typically integrate our recommendations into their onboarding playbooks so customers get good unit economics.
[05:19] Michael Chen: Nice. On security— SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS — what are the common asks?
[05:27] Priya Patel: Most enterprises want SOC2 Type II, TLS+KMS for keys, and audit logs preserved. We support integration with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) for key material. For audit logs, we can stream to your security lake; retention is configurable.
[05:44] Sofia Ruiz: From legal, we'll need to see your SOC2 report and sample DPA. Also curious about data residency and any co-mingling language in reseller agreements.
[05:55] Alex Nguyen: We'll share SOC2 and the security pack; on reseller language we can draft a template that includes data segregation for private deployments.
[06:05] Michael Chen: What about support SLAs? Partners need clear escalation.
[06:11] Sam Carter: We offer SLA tiers on Dedicated and Private. Hosted API has standard and premium SLA tiers with latency and uptime targets, and partners can buy dedicated capacity with SLA-backed throughput. We'll outline options in the partner brief.
[06:26] Ibrahim Al-Karim: For the pilot, what would Redwood want us to run? We could spin up a small test pool.
[06:33] Priya Patel: Suggested pilot: 1) run a couple of generation models (13B quant and a 70B fp16) to test latency and throughput, 2) run an embedding workload for throughput, and 3) validate peering and KMS integration. We can provide a benchmark harness and sample prompts.
[06:52] Michael Chen: We can provision a 6-node test pool (mix of H100 + A800). We'll share exact specs. Ibrahim will own that.
[06:59] Ibrahim Al-Karim: Yep, will compile and send inventory. We may need to rotate drivers so there's a small maintenance window.
[07:06] Laura Gomez: About billing: if we resell, is there an API to pull usage for monthly invoicing or do you prefer a reconciliation file?
[07:17] Alex Nguyen: We have both. Redwood exposes a metering API and we can also provide daily usage exports. For reseller setups we commonly do a consolidated monthly invoice + usage exports for auditability.
[07:30] Michael Chen: Competitors: We run pilots with Lambda and CoreWeave, and we've seen some gaps in the billing integrations. Hoping Redwood has smoother flows.
[07:40] Alex Nguyen: Good to know. We'll map the billing flows and show how partners can access the metering API, webhooks, or SFTP exports.
[07:46] Sofia Ruiz: A practical legal question — for channel reseller agreements, where does liability sit for data breaches? We prefer limited liability on our side but need clear support obligations from Redwood.
[07:58] Alex Nguyen: Understood, partners often want that carve-out. We have standard channel terms; happy to share and iterate.
[08:06] Priya Patel: Quick technical nuance: if you want to run mixed-precision quantization on older A100s, some kernels use vendor-optimized libs and perf can vary; we'd recommend specific firmware/driver combos. We'll include those in the checklist.
[08:22] Ibrahim Al-Karim: Great. On the topic of install — do you provide an infra-as-code module or helm charts?
[08:29] Priya Patel: Yes, for private we provide Terraform modules + Helm charts. For partner-managed nodes, we give scripts plus AMI recommendations. There's a light agent for health checks.
[08:40] Laura Gomez: Perfect. Could you share those artifacts?
[08:44] Priya Patel: We'll attach them in the follow-up.
[08:48] Michael Chen: Anything around certification? Partners sometimes want a short validation test we can run to certify nodes to be Redwood-compatible.
[08:58] Sam Carter: We do a partner validation checklist — once you pass, we list the pool as Redwood-compatible. That helps customers trust the integration. We'll include that in the one-pager.
[09:10] Michael Chen: Nice. Timeline — we're aiming to have two pilot customers ingesting by late Q1 2027. Is that feasible?
[09:18] Alex Nguyen: That's reasonable. If NDA and pilot scope align, we can aim for a technical deep-dive and a benchmark in December, pilot onboarding in January, and limited customer pilots by late Jan/Feb.
[09:29] Sofia Ruiz: I'll review NDA language but expect we'll sign quickly if the liability terms are acceptable.
[09:34] Priya Patel: One practical checklist item for the deep-dive: network diag, driver matrix, AMI IDs, and a sample benchmark workload.
[09:45] Ibrahim Al-Karim: We'll prepare that.
[09:48] Alex Nguyen: Any other blockers?
[09:50] Laura Gomez: One question — on model weights, licensing for certain closed weights. If a customer requests hosted weights, how do we handle licensing and compliance?
[10:02] Priya Patel: For third-party closed models, licensing is per-customer: if the customer has a license, we can deploy; otherwise use open models in our catalog. We'll clarify the flows.
[10:12] Michael Chen: Okay — sounds workable.
[10:15] Alex Nguyen: Alright let's recap and next steps. We'll send NDA and partner one-pager, Priya will send the integration checklist and Terraform/Helm artifacts, Ibrahim will send hardware inventory and availability, and Michael & Sam will draft commercial options.
[10:30] Michael Chen: Yep, will target those dates.
[10:35] Sofia Ruiz: I'll review NDA and follow up with redlines if needed.
[10:40] Alex Nguyen: Great. We'll set up the technical deep-dive invite — I'll propose two slots next week. Is there anything else before we wrap?
[10:50] Laura Gomez: Nothing else from us. Thanks everyone.
[10:53] Alex Nguyen: Thanks, talk soon.
